A new Counterpoint Research report shows that Apple, Garmin, and Huawei grew against the overall decline in smartwatch shipments in Q2 2026, with Huawei reaching a record-high share of global shipments. Details are as follows.

Apple recorded growth across all regions

A new report released yesterday by Counterpoint Research indicated that global smartwatch shipments in Q2 2026 fell 4% year-on-year.

The report noted that Apple saw the largest growth, with shipments rising 14% year-on-year, accounting for 20.1% of global smartwatch shipments and maintaining its position as the world's second largest, just behind Huawei. Huawei's shipments grew 1% year-on-year, with a market share of 21.8%.

Close behind was Imoo, which, despite a 3% year-on-year decline in shipments, still held a 7.8% share; Xiaomi ranked fourth with a 6.1% share, with shipments plunging 38%. Garmin's shipments grew 11%, holding a 5.6% share; the remaining brands together accounted for the remaining 38.5% share, with shipments falling 8% year-on-year.

The report also mentioned that Apple was the fastest-growing of the top five brands in the Chinese market this quarter, "showing that Apple is recovering after a decline in the same period in 2025," with local consumer electronics subsidy programmes also helping to drive smartwatch sales.
